gap: Replace the faceted card-like vegetation and broad polygon verge patches with continuous, depth-layered natural terrain materials and varied grounded silhouettes so every camera reads as a connected landscape rather than a tiled low-poly field.

Cockpit framing and interior geometry are still a stylized dashboard block with no convincing mirror/A-pillar relationship to the road.
Winter and wide-vista shots lack the bar's coherent large-scale landform/water context and realistic snow or aerial-perspective layering.
Vehicle and road markings are recognizable but remain simplified and less physically grounded than the photographic bar composition.

evidence.note: B (bar) has continuous rolling meadow and dense natural vegetation; A (ours) has hard-edged pale verge polygons and repeated faceted clumps despite a readable road/car layout.
B (bar) has a rich warm low-sun landscape and textured road; A (ours) is washed out around the sun with cool flat verge material and stylized foliage.
B (bar) establishes a dark coastal road with strong headlight beam and silhouette depth; A (ours) has a visible beam but low-poly vegetation and a flat, clipped night field.
A (bar) has a believable A-pillar, mirror, road perspective, and restrained overcast contrast; B (ours) is dominated by a chunky dark dashboard and simplified autumn cards.
B (bar) is a coherent open snow landscape with long guardrail and soft terrain; A (ours) keeps recognizable road and snow palette but exposes polygon seams, sparse cards, and dark trunks.
B (bar) delivers a layered lake-and-ridge vista with a small car; A (ours) is an elevated road/bridge over a shallow green field with no comparable atmospheric depth.

verdict_text: Independent round-18 seven-shot blind review: the official bar wins all seven randomized comparisons and the side call is correct 7/7. Road shoulder blending and snow seams are visible improvements, but the dominant read is still low-poly procedural scenery: faceted repeated vegetation, hard verge polygons, and missing continuous landform depth. Lighting/exposure and cockpit geometry remain clear secondary mismatches.
